findings.body:
Turning off `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` makes `identity()` accept any JWT-shaped payload with no proof of issuance. Anyone who can call a route that uses this function can forge claims (user id, roles, tenant) and authenticate as any principal.

The comment cites staging re-issuance (TICKET-412), but nothing in this function scopes the bypass to staging—so the same insecure decode would run in every environment that loads this module.

Restore signature and claim checks:

```suggestion
    return jwt.decode(
        token,
        SECRET,
        algorithms=["HS256"],
        audience="api",
        issuer="accounts.internal.example",
    )
```

If staging must accept a transitional issuer/key, verify against the new key set (or multiple issuers) explicitly rather than disabling verification.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification in `identity()`, so any forged token is accepted as a valid identity.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` trusts the token payload with no cryptographic check and no remaining audience/issuer binding. An attacker who can hit any endpoint that calls `identity()` can mint an unsigned (or arbitrarily signed) JWT with any `sub`/roles/claims and pass auth.

The PR framing (“staging tokens”, TICKET-412) does not limit the blast radius: there is no environment guard, feature flag, or staging-only branch in the diff. As written, the same code path would ship wherever this module is deployed.

## What to do instead

Restore verification (`SECRET`, `algorithms=["HS256"]`, `audience`, `issuer`), and fix staging by re-issuing tokens or rotating to the post-migration signing key/issuer—not by turning verification off. If a temporary staging bypass is unavoidable, gate it explicitly on a non-production runtime check and keep signature verification on whenever a key is available.

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: auth.py identity() now calls jwt.decode with verify_signature/verify_aud/verify_iss all False and no key, audience, or issuer; base still verified HS256 with SECRET, audience, and issuer. The staging comment does not gate the bypass, so forged JWTs are accepted in every environment.
